correctness.rationale: For a word of integer value v and H=2^h, a bit-window occurrence at position j is exactly the disjoint integer intervals [2^j(Hq+v), 2^j(Hq+v+1)-1], q>=0. For strict interior H/2<v<H-1, counting all j windows below m=v+1, n=H+v+1, m+n=H+2v+2 gives offset 0 contributions (1,2,2), offset 1 (0,2,2), and offsets >=2 none: 4v>=m+n and 2H+v>=m+n close the interval checks. Thus defect=4-1-4=-1 uniformly for all h>=3. The count of words is 2^(h-1)-2, with excluded endpoints not assessed. An independent direct canonical substring-count and bit-window program verified all 240 strict-interior patterns h=3..8; finite test not substituted for interval proof.
residual_risks: Leading-zero words require different conventions; endpoints 10^(h-1),1^h intentionally not claimed; zero representation does not add occurrences of leading-one words.

Published all-one positive theorem applies only to excluded endpoint 1^h.

The explicit uniform all-length obstruction is neither a corollary of those distributional results nor known-table recomputation on reviewed sources. Best-of-knowledge with bounded coverage.

value.rationale: A uniform obstruction for all 2^(h-1)-2 nonextremal leading-one binary blocks is a meaningful boundary result in the Graham-style summatory digit inequality problem. The explicit universal witness separates the two genuinely special endpoint candidates, rather than merely computing an arbitrary small exception or taking a limit without motivation.
residual_risks: No determination is made for 10^(h-1) or for words with leading zeros, hence this is not a full all-word classification.

final_claim: For every length h>=3 leading-one binary word except 10^(h-1) and 1^h, its canonical binary occurrence-count summatory F_w(N)=sum_{0<=t<N} c_w(t) violates superadditivity at the explicit m=v+1,n=2^h+v+1, with F(m)=1,F(n)=4,F(m+n)=4 and defect -1.
limitations: The classification is only of the strict-interior leading-one failures, not either endpoint and not leading-zero words. Exact interval proof, not finite tests, establishes all h.
